Analysing every job on the spot takes time. Field mode separates observation from assessment.

  1. On the Field page, choose the workstation and task (you can leave them blank if you don’t know and choose later with “Edit”).
  2. Take a picture with the phone camera or choose from the gallery with 📷 Photo. You can add several photos.
  3. If you shot a video, open it with 🎞 Grab frame from video, go to the important moments and press “Add this frame”. Frames are stored with their video time.
  4. Mark the hazards you see (lifting, pushing-pulling, repetitive work…). If you know them, enter the load, repetitions per shift and task time.
  5. Add a note. You can dictate with the microphone on the phone keyboard.
  6. “Save field record”. The record goes to the Awaiting analysis list.

Back at your desk, the record in the list shows method buttons based on the hazards you marked (e.g. Lifting → NIOSH, KIM-LHC). Pressing a button selects the workstation/task and copies the load and frequency into the form. The “Posture” button on a photo opens that frame in posture analysis. The analyses you save are linked to the field record; when you’re done, mark it “Completed”.

Photos are stored in the browser database on the device (IndexedDB) and never uploaded. Only thumbnails go into the JSON backup.

<p>Duruş analizinde bir video açınca oyn:
When you open a video in posture analysis, “Scan video” below the player takes frames from start to end at the interval you choose (e.g. every 2 seconds), finds the points automatically in each frame and saves them with REBA, RULA and OWAS results to the selected task.

  • Why: A single frame shows a single moment. Frames taken at regular intervals represent the whole job (the OWAS sampling approach). On the Workstations page, the task's time chart and the share of high-risk time in the shift are calculated from these frames.
  • Choose the task first: Records go to the workstation and task selected in the box. If the task duration is entered, risky time is also given in minutes.
  • Interval: 1–2 seconds for fast, short-cycle work; 5–10 seconds for slow work. A shorter interval means more records and a longer scan.
  • Load and side: The load and side entered are applied to all frames. Observations such as twisting, side bending and repetition cannot be detected automatically; open important frames and add them by hand if needed.
  • Checking: Frames in which no person is found are skipped and counted. Automatic points can slip; open and check the worst frames. If you are not happy, “Undo this scan” deletes all records of the scan.
  • Privacy and size: The image never leaves your device. Only a small thumbnail is stored with each record; if the full frame is needed, it is taken again from the video when you open the record with the same video loaded.
Senaryo dene: “şunu değiştirsem ne olur?: Try a scenario: “what if I change this?”
<p>Formlarda ve duruş analizinde sonucun:
In the forms and in posture analysis, the “Try a scenario” button below the result fixes the current values. You can then change the values to see how an action would affect the result, without saving.

  1. First enter the current state (or open a saved analysis), then press “Try a scenario”.
  2. Change the values as if the action were in place: e.g. reduce the load from 25 to 15 kg, raise the lifting height, lower the frequency; in posture analysis type an angle or change the observation boxes.
  3. The table shows the current state and the scenario side by side: score, risk level and which inputs changed.
  4. “Keep” adds the scenario to the list and returns the form to the current state, so you can compare several options (e.g. a pallet lifter versus a two-person lift).
  5. “+ Action” turns the scenario into an action. The action card shows the result expected in the scenario; after the action is in place, “Re-measure” records the real result and compares it with the expected one. In forms, the re-measurement opens with the scenario's values.
  6. “Exit scenario” returns the form to the current values. Nothing is saved in scenario mode.

Scenarios are kept only for this session; turn a scenario you want to keep into an action. A scenario is an estimate: in reality the action may not change the values as much, so re-measurement is essential.
<p>Duruş analizinde kare seçtikten sonra:
In posture analysis, after picking a frame, the “Find points automatically” button finds the person's joints in the image and places the eight points; the angles and REBA, RULA and OWAS are calculated straight away.

  • Privacy: The image never leaves your device. In the web version only the recognition model (MediaPipe Pose, about 10 MB) is downloaded from the internet on first use; in the desktop version the model is built in.
  • Side and direction: If “Side assessed” is selected, that side is used; otherwise the side better visible to the camera. The direction the person faces is also set automatically.
  • Checking is essential: The model estimates from a two-dimensional image. The hand, wrist and ear are the points that slip most often; if the person faces the camera or part of the body is hidden, the angles will be wrong. Check every point and drag it if needed.
  • Points that are not found stay empty; place them by hand.
<p>İstasyonlar sayfasındaki bölge tablos:
The region table on the Workstations page shows how much each task loads six body regions (neck, back-lower back, shoulder-upper arm, elbow-forearm, hand-wrist, leg-knee). Levels come from the task's current records:

  • Posture analysis: REBA component scores (trunk, neck, upper arm, forearm, wrist, legs). A region whose angle was not measured stays empty.
  • QEC: the method's own levels for back, shoulder-arm, hand-wrist and neck.
  • Other forms: the method's result is written to the regions the method assesses (e.g. NIOSH and KIM lifting → back-lower back; OCRA → shoulder, elbow, hand-wrist; ROSA → neck, back, hand-wrist).
  • Nordic questionnaire: the share of people reporting complaints in the last 12 months or last 7 days, on a separate row.

Job rotation plan: Select the tasks to include in the rotation. The app looks for an order in which two consecutive tasks do not load the same region at a high or very high level (with up to 8 tasks, every order is tried) and marks problem transitions. It warns if a region is high in all tasks or a task is very high: in that case rotation does not reduce the risk, it only spreads it to more people. Rotation is an administrative measure; improve the task itself first.
<p>Önlemler sayfasındaki hesap, önlemler:
The calculation on the Actions page compares the budget for actions with the annual cost of musculoskeletal disorders.

  • Case cost = lost work days per case × cost of one work day + other direct cost (treatment, transport, administration).
  • Annual cost = cases per year × case cost × (1 + indirect cost multiplier). Indirect costs (replacement staff, overtime, lost productivity and quality) are often larger than direct costs, but they vary a lot between workplaces; leave 0 if unknown.
  • Saving = annual cost × expected reduction from the actions; payback period = cost of actions ÷ annual saving.
  • If the cost of actions is left empty, the sum of the estimated costs entered on the actions is used.
  • The figures are your estimates, so the result is not exact; state the assumptions when presenting to management. Improvements verified by re-measurement are a good basis for the expected reduction.
<p>İstasyonlar sayfasındaki tablo, her i:
The table on the Workstations page makes each risk area of each workstation a row. Choose Fine-Kinney or the 5×5 matrix with the button at the top.

  • Suggested values: probability comes from the method’s risk level, frequency from the task duration (120 min or more per shift is “continuous”), severity from the type of hazard.
  • Adjust: with “Edit”, change the hazard, possible harm, probability, frequency and severity to suit the site. A changed row is marked “manually corrected”; undo with “Back to suggested values”.
  • The scale values are taken from common practice; compare them with your own organisation’s table.
<p>Görevlerin vardiyadaki sürelerini (dk: When you enter the tasks’ durations per shift (min), the workstation card shows the shift profile: each task’s share of the shift, the time-weighted share of high-risk postures (REBA and OWAS) and a sub-activity table for the other methods. Tasks without a duration are weighted equally, and the screen says so.
Sonuçları doğru okumak: sınırlar ve dikk: Reading the results correctly: limits and points to watch
<ul>\n <li><b>Tek kare, tek an:</b> REB:
• One frame, one moment: REBA and RULA score a momentary posture. To represent a task, save the most demanding moment and the most frequent or longest-held posture separately; the workstation card shows the worst value.
  • Angles measured from images: If the camera is not side-on and perpendicular, angles deviate. Angles close to a threshold that changes the score are marked “borderline”; check them with a goniometer.
  • What the image can’t show: Load weight, twisting, side bending, arm abduction and wrist deviation are not visible from the side. If you don’t mark them under Observations, the score comes out low.
  • Scope of the methods: Methods such as NIOSH, RULA and REBA were developed for healthy adult workers. For young, pregnant or breastfeeding, disabled workers or those with complaints, limits should be kept lower; assess with the occupational physician.
  • Methods don’t replace each other: REBA is for the whole body, RULA for the upper limb, NIOSH for lifting, OCRA for repetitive work. If a job has several risks, use the suitable method for each; the Guide shows which are needed.
  • Before-after comparison: After an action, re-measure the same task with the same method and a similar frame; scores from different methods are not comparable.
<p>Türkiye’de ergonomik riskler, işveren:
In Turkey, ergonomic risks are part of the risk assessment that employers are obliged to carry out. The main regulations are:

  • Occupational Health and Safety Law No. 6331 (20.06.2012): the employer must carry out or commission a risk assessment.
  • Regulation on Occupational Health and Safety Risk Assessment (Official Gazette 29.12.2012, No. 28512): the assessment is carried out by a team set up by the employer, including the occupational safety specialist, the occupational physician, the employee representative and workers who know the job.
  • Regulation on Manual Handling Work (Official Gazette 24.07.2013, No. 28717): measures in manual handling, especially against back and low-back injuries.
  • Regulation on Health and Safety Measures for Work with Display Screen Equipment (Official Gazette 16.04.2013, No. 28620): computer work; ROSA can be used in this context.

Where Duruş fits: These regulations are aligned with the corresponding EU directives (89/391/EEC, 90/269/EEC, 90/270/EEC); outside Turkey, follow your own national legislation. Duruş’s results provide input and decision support for risk assessment; on their own they are not an official risk assessment or a medical assessment. Interpret the results with the assessment team, especially the occupational safety specialist and occupational physician. For the current text of the legislation, consult official sources (mevzuat.gov.tr, Official Gazette).
